programme.title: Storyville
programme.desc: In August 2020, a plane travelling from Siberia to Moscow made an emergency landing. One of its passengers, Russian opposition leader Alexei Navalny, was deathly ill. Taken to a local Siberian hospital and eventually evacuated to Berlin, doctors there confirmed that he had been poisoned with Novichok, a nerve agent implicated in attacks on other opponents of the Russian government. President Vladimir Putin immediately cast doubt on the findings and denied any involvement.

programme.title: Talking Pictures
programme.desc: Celia Imrie celebrates the cinema's marvellous movie musicals, venturing back through the BBC's archives to look at film's most joyous and arguably enduring genre. Interviews with some of the biggest stars and directors take us from the golden age of icons like Marilyn Monro, Jane Russell, Gene Kelly and Fred Astaire to the modern day triumphs of La La Land and The Greatest Showman. The programme also explores the connection between the box office charts and the music charts.

programme.title: Eden: Untamed Planet
programme.desc: Borneo is the richest rainforest island of all, home to 60,000 species of plants and animals. Six thousand of them are unique, and more are discovered almost daily. But this `paradise' is an illusion, the lush forest is effectively growing on a desert, with the soil shallow and poor in nutrients, having been leeched by eons of incessant rain.

programme.title: Florence Nightingale: Nursing Pioneer
programme.desc: A look at the life of Florence Nightingale, a trailblazer who revolutionised modern nursing. Born into a rich English family, Nightingale broke through social and gender barriers to pioneer a profession previously reserved for men.

programme.title: Mysteries of the Bayeux Tapestry
programme.desc: The Bayeux Tapestry is a remarkable and unique work of art that has survived for almost 1,000 years. Made in the 11th century, it tells the story of William of Normandy's claim to the English throne, culminating in the Norman invasion of England and the Battle of Hastings.

programme.title: Michael Palin: The Art of Travel

programme.title: Calamity Jane
programme.desc: Indian scout Calamity Jane is as handy with a gun as any man in Deadwood, Dakota Territory. When sent to Chicago to recruit an actress for the Golden Garter stage, the woman proves to be a more feminine rival for the attentions of Jane's male friends, including Wild Bill Hickok.

programme.title: Top of the Pops
programme.desc: Mike Read introduces performances from Linx, Bucks Fizz, Saxon, Keith Marshall, Graham Bonnet, Public Image Ltd., Eddy Grant, Gillan, The Whispers, Hazel O'Connor and Shakin' Stevens. Also includes a dance performance by Legs & Co.

programme.title: The Old Grey Whistle Test
programme.desc: Blondie perform live at the height of their powers in 1979 at the Apollo Theatre in Glasgow, with Debbie Harry wowing the audience with such hits as `Dreaming', `Union City Blue', `Picture This', `Heart of Glass', `Hanging on the Telephone' and `Sunday Girl'.

programme.title: Shirley Bassey at the BBC: Volume Two
programme.desc: A collection of Shirley Bassey's performances from the BBC archives, including such hits as `My Way', `The Way We Were', `Copacabana' and even her own version of the Beatles' iconic `Hey Jude'.

programme.title: Shirley Bassey at the Royal Albert Hall 1974
programme.desc: Shirley Bassey performs iconic songs at the Royal Albert Hall in London in 1974.

programme.title: Imagine...
programme.sub-title: Dame Shirley Bassey: The Girl from Tiger Bay
programme.desc: Alan Yentob gains exclusive access and insight into the creative world of Dame Shirley as she tentatively re-enters the ring to confront her life in song. Some of the best contemporary songwriters, including Gary Barlow, Manic Street Preachers, Rufus Wainwright and famous Bond composer John Barry, have interpreted her life through song for a new album produced by David Arnold.

programme.title: Dame Shirley Bassey: Electric Proms
programme.desc: Trevor Nelson and Edith Bowman present highlights of Dame Shirley Bassey's special performance for the `Electric Proms' from London's Roundhouse. The British icon performs a set packed with classic tracks like `Big Spender' and `Goldfinger' and premieres new songs from her forthcoming album, `The Performance', produced by Bond composer David Arnold.

programme.title: Is Greenland for Sale?
programme.desc: US president Donald Trump says he wants the US to take over Greenland. The country is part of the Kingdom of Denmark, and Mr Trump says Denmark should 'give it up' for the defence of the free world. Many people think it will never happen. But could it? If so, how? In this programme, we hear what Mr Trump has said. We gauge the reaction in Greenland and Denmark. And we ask why the US might want greater control over Greenland, and how likely it is to happen.
